title: Salvation and Obedience
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Salvation and obedience teaches that true salvation produces a life increasingly submitted to Jesus Christ. Obedience does not purchase salvation, but it does reveal the living faith of those who belong to Him.
summary: Salvation and obedience teaches that true salvation produces a life increasingly submitted to Jesus Christ. Obedience does not purchase salvation, but it does reveal the living faith of those who belong to Him.
christFocus: Jesus Christ saves sinners and calls them to follow Him as Lord. He does not merely pardon rebellion; He brings His people into loving obedience under His rule.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The Gospel must never be twisted into salvation by works. Yet it must also never be twisted into a message that leaves people comfortable in rebellion.

Jesus calls His disciples to obey Him. Love for Christ is shown through keeping His commandments, not as payment for salvation but as the fruit of belonging to Him.

Grace trains believers to renounce ungodliness and live godly lives. Salvation changes allegiance. The believer is brought out of slavery to sin and into obedience from the heart.

Obedience remains imperfect in this life, and believers continue needing mercy. But a settled refusal to obey Christ contradicts the claim of saving faith.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some fear that talking about obedience will weaken grace, while others use obedience to crush people under performance. Scripture keeps grace and obedience in their proper order.

This doctrine helps believers see that Christ saves them as Lord. He is not an accessory to life, but the King who calls His people into joyful submission.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Obey Christ from faith and love, not fear of earning acceptance. When you fail, repent and return to Him. Do not use grace to excuse disobedience, and do not use obedience to boast. Let salvation produce a life increasingly surrendered to the Lord who saved you.
